newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric steady after bid defence.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric steady after bid defence.

text.p: Shares in Northern Electric Plc were unchanged on Friday after the company set out key elements of its defence against the hostile bid from CalEnergy Co of the U.S., including a falling level of debt.
The shares remained at yesterday's closing level of 590p by 0934 GMT, in thin trading of 14,830 shares.

Northern Electric forecast gearing of around 95 percent at March 31, after payment of a special dividend promised in its last bid defence. Net debt of about 240 million stg would be some 47 million lower than average market estimates, it said.
Some analysts believe these forecasts will aid Northern Electric's defence against CalEnergy's bid of 630p per share.
"I believe the bid from CalEnergy undervalues Northern Electric and these forecasts underpin this judgement," said one analyst.
"The company is worth something around 670p, if you exclude the bid premium and shareholders should hold out for something nearer 700p."

Northern reported first-half pre-tax profits of 50.7 million stg against 58.7 million stg last time, but the statement on the financial position of the company in light of the bid from CalEnergy Co Inc was more signficant, dealers said.
"Today's results were not about profits but about the financial state of Northern Electric," said one sales trader. "Gearing is falling and that is good news."
A spokesman for CE Electric, 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, said Northern's results were "lacklustre."
